Profile Dried yeast consists of unicellular fungi belonging to the family Saccharomycetaceae, dried by a process that avoids decomposi- tion of the vitamins present. The chief species are Saccharomy- ces cerevisiae, S. carlsbergensis, and S. monacensis. Dried yeast contains thiamine, nicotinic acid, riboflavin, pyridoxine, pan- tothenic acid, biotin, folic acid, cyanocobalamin, aminobenzoic acid, inositol, and chromium. Dried yeast is a rich source of vitamins of the B group. It has been used for the prevention and treatment of vitamin B deficiency in doses of 1 to 8 g daily by mouth. Yeast is an ingredient of some preparations for treating haemorrhoids, and some preparations intended to restore normal gastrointestinal flora. Yeast is widely used in brewing.
